entries.sanskrit:
अष्टमे तु तपश्-चर्या मार्कण्डेयस्य मोहकैः ।

कामादिभिर् असम्मोहो नर-नारायण-स्तुतिः ॥

पुराण-विभाग-प्रसङ्गेन पुराण-कर्तुर् मार्कण्डेयस्य चरित-प्रश्नम् आह--सूतेति । त्वम् एव वक्तुं योग्य इत्य् आह--तमसि संसारे भ्रमतां पार-दर्शनस् तन्-निवर्तकः ॥१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्री-शौनक उवाच—

सूत जीव चिरं साधो वद नो वदतां वर ।  
तमस्य् अपारे भ्रमतां नॄणां त्वं पार-दर्शनः ॥
entries.transliteration:
śrī-śaunaka uvāca—

sūta jīva ciraṃ sādho vada no vadatāṃ vara |
tamasy apāre bhramatāṃ nṝṇāṃ tvaṃ pāra-darśanaḥ ||
entries.literal_english: In the eighth chapter are described Mārkaṇḍeya’s austerity, his freedom from delusion caused by Cupid and the other enchantments, and the praise of Nara-Nārāyaṇa. In the context of dividing the Purāṇas, the question about the history of Mārkaṇḍeya, the author of the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, is introduced with “Sūta.” You alone are fit to speak; “in darkness” means in the worldly existence, and “showing the far shore” means the remover of those who wander in it.

entries.sanskrit: वक्तव्यम् आह—आहुर् इति । उर्वरितोऽवशिष्टः । येन कल्पान्तेन । एतत् कथं घटते ? इत्य् एकः प्रश्नः ॥२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
आहुश् चिरायुषम् ऋषिं मृकण्डु-तनयं जनाः ।  
यः कल्पान्ते ह्य् उर्वरितो येन ग्रस्तम् इदं जगत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
āhuś cirāyuṣam ṛṣiṃ mṛkaṇḍu-tanayaṃ janāḥ |
yaḥ kalpānte hy urvarito yena grastam idaṃ jagat ||
word_for_word: at the end of the kalpa
entries.literal_english: He states what is to be told with “they say.” “Urvarita” means remaining, and “by which” means by the end of the kalpa. One question is: how can this situation occur?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: प्रलयाभावाद् अप्य् एतन् न घटत इत्य् आह—स वा इति । यतो भार्गव-र्षभः । कोऽपि प्राकृतिको नैमित्तिको वा ॥३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
स वा अस्मत्-कुलोत्पन्नः कल्पेऽस्मिन् भार्गव-र्षभः ।  
नैवाधुनापि भूतानां सम्प्लवः कोऽपि जायते ॥
entries.transliteration:
sa vā asmat-kulotpannaḥ kalpe’smin bhārgava-rṣabhaḥ |
naivādhunāpi bhūtānāṃ samplavaḥ ko’pi jāyate ||
entries.literal_english: He says that this does not fit even because there is no annihilation: “He is the foremost Bhārgava.” “Any” means either a natural or an occasional dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: अन्यद् अप्य् अघटितम् एवेत्य् आह—एक एवेति । तोकं बालकम् ॥४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
एक एवार्णवे भ्राम्यन् ददर्श पुरुषं किल ।  
वट-पत्र-पुटे तोकं शयानं त्व् एकम् अद्भुतम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
eka evārṇave bhrāmyan dadarśa puruṣaṃ kila |
vaṭa-patra-puṭe tokaṃ śayānaṃ tv ekam adbhutam ||
word_for_word: within the fold of a banyan leaf
entries.literal_english: He says that another extraordinary matter also does not fit: “One alone.” “Tokam” means a child.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
एष नः संशयो भूयान् सूत कौतूहलं यतः ।  
तं नश् छिन्धि महा-योगिन् पुराणेष्व् अपि सम्मतः ॥
entries.transliteration:
eṣa naḥ saṃśayo bhūyān sūta kautūhalaṃ yataḥ |
taṃ naś chindhi mahā-yogin purāṇeṣv api sammataḥ ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: प्रश्नम् अभिनन्दति—हे महर्षे । अयं प्रश्नः । तत्र हेतुः—नारायणेति । यत्र प्रश्न-विषये ॥६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सूत उवाच—

प्रश्नस् त्वया महर्षेऽयं कृतो लोक-भ्रमापहः ।  
नारायण-कथा यत्र गीता कलि-मलापहा ॥
entries.transliteration:
sūta uvāca—

praśnas tvayā maharṣe’yaṃ kṛto loka-bhramāpahaḥ |
nārāyaṇa-kathā yatra gītā kali-malāpahā ||
entries.literal_english: He praises the question: “O great sage, this question.” Its reason is stated by “Nārāyaṇa”: the question concerns the topics in which the story of Nārāyaṇa is spoken.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र मार्कण्डेयस् तपसा भगवन्तम् आराध्य माया-प्रदर्शनं वव्रे । ततश् च तेनैव भगवन्-मायया सप्त-कल्पा दृष्टा नान्यैर् इत्य् उत्तरं वक्तुम् आदित आरभ्य तस्य चरितम् आह—प्राप्त इत्य्-आदिना । मार्कण्डेयो मृत्युं जिग्ये इति पञ्चम-श्लोकेनान्वयः । मध्यम-ग्रन्थेन तस्य धर्मः कथ्यते । प्राप्तो द्वि-जाति-संस्कार उपनयनाख्यो येन सः । पितुः सकाशाद् गर्भाधानादि-क्रमात् । छन्दांसि वेदान् ॥७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
प्राप्त-द्वि-जाति-संस्कारो मार्कण्डेयः पितुः क्रमात् ।  
छन्दांस्य् अधीत्य धर्मेण तपः-स्वाध्याय-संयुतः ॥
entries.transliteration:
prāpta-dvi-jāti-saṃskāro mārkaṇḍeyaḥ pituḥ kramāt |
chandāṃsy adhītya dharmeṇa tapaḥ-svādhyāya-saṃyutaḥ ||
word_for_word: in due order from his father
endowed with austerity and Vedic study
entries.literal_english: Mārkaṇḍeya worshiped the Lord through austerity and asked Him to display His Māyā. By that very divine Māyā he saw seven kalpas, unlike anyone else; therefore Śrīdhara begins the answer by narrating his history. The connection is with the fifth verse: Mārkaṇḍeya conquered death. His dharma is described in the intervening text. “Having received the second-birth rite” means one who received the upanayana rite; “from the father” means in the sequence beginning with conception and the other rites; “the meters” means the Vedas.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: बृहद्-व्रत-धरो नैष्ठिको ब्रह्मचारी सन् ॥८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
बृहद्-व्रत-धरः शान्तो जटिलो वल्कलाम्बरः ।  
बिभ्रत् कमण्डलुं दण्डम् उपवीतं स-मेखलम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
bṛhad-vrata-dharaḥ śānto jaṭilo valkalāmbaraḥ |
bibhrat kamaṇḍaluṃ daṇḍam upavītaṃ sa-mekhalam ||
entries.literal_english: “Holder of the great vow” means that he was a lifelong celibate student.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: नियम-र्द्धये धर्म-वृद्धये अग्न्य्-आदिषु पञ्चसु हरिम् अर्चयन् ॥९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कृष्णाजिनं साक्ष-सूत्रं कुशांश् च नियमर्द्धये ।  
अग्न्य्-अर्क-गुरु-विप्रात्मस्व् अर्चयन् सन्ध्ययोर् हरिम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
kṛṣṇājinaṃ sākṣa-sūtraṃ kuśāṃś ca niyamarddhaye |
agny-arka-guru-viprātmasv arcayan sandhyayor harim ||
word_for_word: in fire, sun, guru, brāhmaṇas and the Self
at the two junctures of day
entries.literal_english: “For the increase of discipline” means for the growth of religious practice. He worshiped Hari in the five forms of fire, sun, guru, brāhmaṇas and the indwelling Self.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: भैक्ष्यं गुर्व्-अर्थम् आहृत्य तेनानुज्ञातश् चेत् तर्हि बुभुजे नो चेत् सकृत् कदाचिद् उपोषितो भवति ॥१०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सायं प्रातः स गुरवे भैक्ष्यम् आहृत्य वाग्-यतः ।  
बुभुजे गुर्व्-अनुज्ञातः सकृन् नो चेद् उपोषितः ॥
entries.transliteration:
sāyaṃ prātaḥ sa gurave bhaikṣyam āhṛtya vāg-yataḥ |
bubhuje gurv-anujñātaḥ sakṛn no ced upoṣitaḥ ||
entries.literal_english: He brought the alms for the sake of the guru. If he was permitted by him, he ate; if not, he fasted, sometimes for a single day.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
एवं तपः-स्वाध्याय-परो वर्षाणाम् अयुतायुतम् ।  
आराधयन् हृषीकेशं जिग्ये मृत्युं सु-दुर्जयम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
evaṃ tapaḥ-svādhyāya-paro varṣāṇām ayutāyutam |
ārādhayan hṛṣīkeśaṃ jigye mṛtyuṃ su-durjayam ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: तेन मृत्यु-जयेन ॥१२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मा भृगुर् भवो दक्षो ब्रह्म-पुत्राश् च येऽपरे ।  
नृ-देव-पितृ-भूतानि तेनासन्न् अति-विस्मिताः ॥
entries.transliteration:
brahmā bhṛgur bhavo dakṣo brahma-putrāś ca ye’pare |
nṛ-deva-pitṛ-bhūtāni tenāsann ati-vismitāḥ ||
entries.literal_english: By him who conquered death.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: ध्वस्ताः क्लेशा रागादयो यस्य तेनान्तर्-आत्मना प्रत्याहृत-मनसा ॥१३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
इत्थं बृहद्-व्रत-धरस् तपः-स्वाध्याय-संयमैः ।  
दध्याव् अधोक्षजं योगी ध्वस्त-क्लेशान्तरात्मना ॥
entries.transliteration:
itthaṃ bṛhad-vrata-dharas tapaḥ-svādhyāya-saṃyamaiḥ |
dadhyāv adhokṣajaṃ yogī dhvasta-kleśāntarātmanā ||
entries.literal_english: “With the inner self” means with the mind withdrawn within, because the afflictions such as attachment had been destroyed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यैवं युञ्जतश् चित्तं महा-योगेन योगिनः ।  
व्यतीयाय महान् कालो मन्वन्तर-षड्-आत्मकः ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasyaivaṃ yuñjataś cittaṃ mahā-yogena yoginaḥ |
vyatīyāya mahān kālo manvantara-ṣaḍ-ātmakaḥ ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: तस्य तपो-निष्ठाम् इतिहासेन वर्णयति—एतद् इत्य्-आदिना । अस्मिन् सप्तमे मन्वन्तरे । तपसा मत्-पदं ग्रहीष्यतीति विशङ्कितः ॥१५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
एतत् पुरन्दरो ज्ञात्वा सप्तमेऽस्मिन् किलान्तरे ।  
तपो-विशङ्कितो ब्रह्मन्न् आरेभे तद्-विघातनम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
etat purandaro jñātvā saptame’smin kilāntare |
tapo-viśaṅkito brahmann ārebhe tad-vighātanam ||
entries.literal_english: His firm devotion to austerity is narrated through an historical account. “In this seventh Manvantara” identifies the present period. Indra, fearing that Mārkaṇḍeya would attain the Lord’s position through austerity, became anxious.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: मुनये मुनिं भ्रंशयितुम् । रजसस् तोकम् अतिप्रियम् अपत्यं लोभो मदश् च तौ ॥१६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसः कामं वसन्त-मलयानिलौ ।  
मुनये प्रेषयाम् आस रजस्-तोक-मदौ तथा ॥
entries.transliteration:
gandharvāpsarasaḥ kāmaṃ vasanta-malayānilau |
munaye preṣayām āsa rajas-toka-madau tathā ||
entries.literal_english: He sent them to make the sage fall. “The child of passion” means an exceedingly beloved child of passion; the two others are greed and intoxication.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
ते वै तद्-आश्रमं जग्मुर् हिमाद्रेः पार्श्व उत्तरे ।  
पुष्पभद्रा नदी यत्र चित्राख्या च शिला विभो ॥
entries.transliteration:
te vai tad-āśramaṃ jagmur himādreḥ pārśva uttare |
puṣpabhadrā nadī yatra citrākhyā ca śilā vibho ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: तद्-आश्रम-पदं प्रविष्टो वायुर् ववाव् इति तृतीयेनान्वयः । पुण्यैर् द्रुमैर् लताभिश् चाञ्चितं पूजितम् । पुण्य-द्विजानाम् ऋषीणां कुलैर् आकीर्णम् । पुण्या अमला जलाशया यस्मिन् ॥१८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तद्-आश्रम-पदं पुण्यं पुण्य-द्रुम-लताञ्चितम् ।  
पुण्य-द्विज-कुलाकीर्णं पुण्यामल-जलाशयम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tad-āśrama-padaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇya-druma-latāñcitam |
puṇya-dvija-kulākīrṇaṃ puṇyāmala-jalāśayam ||
entries.literal_english: After entering that hermitage, the wind blew; this is connected with the third verse. It was honored and adorned with virtuous trees and creepers, filled with the groups of virtuous twice-born sages, and had pure, spotless reservoirs of water.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: मत्त-भ्रमराणां सङ्गीतं यस्मिन् । मत्त-कोकिलानां कूजितं यस्मिन् । मत्ता बर्हिण एव नटास् तेषाम् आटोपो नृत्य-संभ्रामो यस्मिन् । मत्तानां पक्षिणा कुलैर् आकुलं व्याप्तम् ॥१९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
मत्त-भ्रमर-सङ्गीतं मत्त-कोकिल-कूजितम् ।  
मत्त-बर्हि-नटाटोपं मत्त-द्विज-कुलाकुलम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
matta-bhramara-saṅgītaṃ matta-kokila-kūjitam |
matta-barhi-naṭāṭopaṃ matta-dvija-kulākulam ||
word_for_word: with the frenzy of dancing peacocks
entries.literal_english: It had the song of intoxicated bees, the cooing of intoxicated cuckoos, the dancing tumult of intoxicated peacocks, and was filled by multitudes of intoxicated birds.

entries.sanskrit: एवं-भूतं तद् आश्रम-पदं प्रविष्टः सन् वायुर् मलयानिलो ववौ प्रससार । उत्तम्भयन्न् उहीपयन् । तत्र वृक्षेषु प्रवेशान् मान्द्यं हिम-निर्झर-कणानाम् आदानाच् छैत्यं पुष्प-परिष्वङ्गात् सौगन्ध्यं चोक्तम् ॥२०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
वायुः प्रविष्ट आदाय हिम-निर्झर-शीकरान् ।  
सुमनोभिः परिष्वक्तो ववाव् उत्तम्भयन् स्मरम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
vāyuḥ praviṣṭa ādāya hima-nirjhara-śīkarān |
sumanobhiḥ pariṣvakto vavāv uttambhayan smaram ||
entries.literal_english: The wind, the Malaya breeze, entered that hermitage and spread. “Awakening” means stirring up. The verse describes the wind’s softness from entering the trees, its coolness from taking up drops from the snowy waterfalls, and its fragrance from embracing the flowers.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, उद्यंश् चन्द्रो यस्मिंस् तन्-निशा-वक्त्रं रजनी-मुखं यस्मिन् सः । प्रवाल-स्तवकानाम् आलयः श्रेणयो येषु तैः । गुप्यन्ति विटपैः संश्लिष्यन्तीति गोपा द्रुमा लताश् च तेषां जालैः समूहैर् उपलक्षित आविर् बभूव ॥२१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
उद्यच्-चन्द्र-निशा-वक्त्रः प्रवाल-स्तबकालिभिः ।  
गोप-द्रुम-लता-जालैस् तत्रासीत् कुसुमाकरः ॥
entries.transliteration:
udyac-candra-niśā-vaktraḥ pravāla-stabakālibhiḥ |
gopa-druma-latā-jālais tatrāsīt kusumākaraḥ ||
word_for_word: whose night-face was the rising moon
with rows of coral-like flower clusters
with networks of trees and creepers
entries.literal_english: Moreover, the face of the night was the face of spring because the rising moon appeared in it. The trees were marked by rows that were abodes of clusters of coral-like blossoms, and the spring became manifest, covered by networks of trees and creepers that clung together.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, तदा गीत-वादित्र-यूथकैर् गायकादि-समुदायिभिर् गन्धर्वैर् अन्वीयमानः । तथा स्वः-स्त्रियोऽप्सरसस् तासां यूथस्य पतिः । आत्तं चापम् इषुश् च येन, स स्मरश् च तत्रादृश्यत ॥२२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अन्वीयमानो गन्धर्वैर् गीत-वादित्र-यूथकैः ।  
अदृश्यतात्त-चापेषुः स्वः-स्त्री-यूथ-पतिः स्मरः ॥
entries.transliteration:
anvīyamāno gandharvair gīta-vāditra-yūthakaiḥ |
adṛśyatātta-cāpeṣuḥ svaḥ-strī-yūtha-patiḥ smaraḥ ||
word_for_word: by groups singing and playing instruments
lord of the groups of heavenly women
entries.literal_english: Then Cupid was seen followed by Gandharvas belonging to groups of singers and instrumentalists. He was the lord of the troop of heavenly women, and he held a bow and an arrow.

entries.sanskrit: दुराधर्षम् अभिभवितुम् अशक्यम् ॥२३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
हुत्वाग्निं समुपासीनं ददृशुः शक्र-किङ्कराः ।  
मीलिताक्षं दुराधर्षं मूर्तिमन्तम् इवानलम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
hutvāgniṃ samupāsīnaṃ dadṛśuḥ śakra-kiṅkarāḥ |
mīlitākṣaṃ durādharṣaṃ mūrtimantam ivānalam ||
entries.literal_english: “Difficult to attack” means impossible to overcome.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
ननृतुस् तस्य पुरतः स्त्रियोऽथो गायका जगुः ।  
मृदङ्ग-वीणा-पणवैर् वाद्यं चक्रुर् मनो-रमम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
nanṛtus tasya purataḥ striyo’tho gāyakā jaguḥ |
mṛdaṅga-vīṇā-paṇavair vādyaṃ cakrur mano-ramam ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.

entries.sanskrit: शोषण-दीपन-सम्मोहन-तापनोन्मादनाख्यानि पञ्च मुखानि यस्य तद्-अस्त्रं सन्दधे । तदैव मधुर् वसन्तः । रजस्-तोकश् च पुंस्त्वम् आर्षम् । अन्ये चेन्द्र-भृत्यास् तस्य मनो व्यकम्पयन् ॥२५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सन्दधेऽस्त्रं स्व-धनुषि कामः पञ्च-मुखं तदा ।  
मधुर् मनो रजस्-तोक इन्द्र-भृत्या व्यकम्पयन् ॥
entries.transliteration:
sandadhe’straṃ sva-dhanuṣi kāmaḥ pañca-mukhaṃ tadā |
madhur mano rajas-toka indra-bhṛtyā vyakampayan ||
entries.literal_english: He fixed on his bow a weapon whose five heads are called drying, kindling, deluding, scorching and maddening. At that very time Spring was present. “The child of passion” means manhood in the archaic usage. The other servants of Indra agitated his mind.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्रीडन्त्याः पुञ्जिकस्थल्याः कन्दुकैः स्तन-गौरवात् ।  
भृशम् उद्विग्न-मध्यायाः केश-विस्रंसित-स्रजः ॥
entries.transliteration:
krīḍantyāḥ puñjikasthalyāḥ kandukaiḥ stana-gauravāt |
bhṛśam udvigna-madhyāyāḥ keśa-visraṃsita-srajaḥ ||
entries.literal_english: No commentary.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, वायुर् मलयानिलः पुञ्जिक-स्थल्यास् तत् सूक्ष्मं वासो जहार ॥२७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
इतस् ततो भ्रमद्-दृष्टेश् चलन्त्या अनु कन्दुकम् ।  
वायुर् जहार तद्-वासः सूक्ष्मं त्रुटित-मेखलम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
itas tato bhramad-dṛṣṭeś calantyā anu kandukam |
vāyur jahāra tad-vāsaḥ sūkṣmaṃ truṭita-mekhalam ||
entries.literal_english: Moreover, the Malaya breeze carried away Puñjikasthalī’s fine garment.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: सर्वं तेषां कर्म । तत्र तस्मिन् । मोघं व्यर्थम् । अनीशस्य निर्दैवस्य ॥२८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
विससर्ज तदा बाणं मत्वा तं स्व-जितं स्मरः ।  
सर्वं तत्राभवन् मोघम् अनीशस्य यथोद्यमः ॥
entries.transliteration:
visasarja tadā bāṇaṃ matvā taṃ sva-jitaṃ smaraḥ |
sarvaṃ tatrābhavan mogham anīśasya yathodyamaḥ ||
entries.literal_english: “All” means all their efforts; “there” means in that situation; “futile” means fruitless; “of one without power” means of one deprived of divine fortune.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: मुनेर् अपकुर्वन्तः प्रतिकूलम् आचरन्तः । हे मुने ॥२९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
त इत्थम् अपकुर्वन्तो मुनेस् तत्-तेजसा मुने ।  
दह्यमाना निववृतुः प्रबोध्याहिम् इवार्भकाः ॥
entries.transliteration:
ta ittham apakurvanto munes tat-tejasā mune |
dahyamānā nivavṛtuḥ prabodhyāhim ivārbhakāḥ ||
entries.literal_english: “Trying to harm the sage” means acting against him. “O sage” is an address to Śaunaka.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: अहमोऽहङ्कारस्य । भावं विकारम् ॥३०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
इतीन्द्रानुचरैर् ब्रह्मन् धर्षितोऽपि महा-मुनिः ।  
यन् नागाद् अहमो भावं न तच् चित्रं महत्सु हि ॥
entries.transliteration:
itīndrānucarair brahman dharṣito’pi mahā-muniḥ |
yan nāgād ahamo bhāvaṃ na tac citraṃ mahatsu hi ||
entries.literal_english: “False ego” means a transformation of the ego-principle.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: निस्तेजसं म्लान-वदनम् । स्व-राड् इन्द्रः ॥३१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा निस्तेजसं कामं स-गणं भगवान् स्वराट् ।  
श्रुत्वानुभावं ब्रह्मर्षेर् विस्मयं समगात् परम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā nistejasaṃ kāmaṃ sa-gaṇaṃ bhagavān svarāṭ |
śrutvānubhāvaṃ brahmarṣer vismayaṃ samagāt param ||
entries.literal_english: “Without potency” means with a faded face. “The self-ruler” is Indra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: नर-नारायण-रूपो हरिः ॥३२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यैवं युञ्जतश् चित्तं तपः-स्वाध्याय-संयमैः ।  
अनुग्रहायाविरासीन् नर-नारायणो हरिः ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasyaivaṃ yuñjataś cittaṃ tapaḥ-svādhyāya-saṃyamaiḥ |
anugrahāyāvirāsīn nara-nārāyaṇo hariḥ ||
entries.literal_english: Hari appeared in the form of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: ताव् अनुवर्णयति द्वाभ्याम्—ताव् इति । रौरवं कृष्णाजिनं वल्कलं चाम्बरं ययोस् तौ । पवित्रे पाण्योर् ययोस् तौ । त्रि-वृत् त्रि-गुणं नव-तन्तुकम् इति वा त्रि-वृद् बहिः पवमानम् इत्य्-आदौ नवके प्रयोगात् । उपवीतकादीन् दधानौ । वेदं दर्भ-मुष्टिम् । किं च, साक्षात् तप एव तौ । तत्र हेतुः, तपत्-ताडिद्-वर्णं देदीप्यमान-विद्युत्-सङ्काशं यत् पिशङ्गं रोचिस् तेन रूपिणौ मूर्तिम् अन्तौ । तादृक्-तेजो-युक्त-मूर्तिभ्यां तपो-मयत्वेन प्रकाशमानाव् इत्य् अर्थः । प्रांशू उन्नतौ ॥३३-३४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तौ शुक्ल-कृष्णौ नव-कञ्ज-लोचनौ

चतुर्-भुजौ रौरव-वल्कलाम्बरौ ।

पवित्र-पाणी उपवीतकं त्रि-वृत्

कमण्डलुं दण्डम् ऋजुं च वैणवम् ॥

पद्माक्ष-मालाम् उत जन्तु-मार्जनं

वेदं च साक्षात् तप एव रूपिणौ ।

तपत्-तडिद्-वर्ण-पिशङ्ग-रोचिषा

प्रांशू दधानौ विबुधर्षभार्चितौ ॥
entries.transliteration:
tau śukla-kṛṣṇau nava-kañja-locanau

catur-bhujau raurava-valkalāmbarau |

pavitra-pāṇī upavītakaṃ tri-vṛt

kamaṇḍaluṃ daṇḍam ṛjuṃ ca vaiṇavam ||

padmākṣa-mālām uta jantu-mārjanaṃ

vedaṃ ca sākṣāt tapa eva rūpiṇau |

tapat-taḍid-varṇa-piśaṅga-rociṣā

prāṃśū dadhānau vibudharṣabhārcitau ||
word_for_word: worshiped by the best of the gods
entries.literal_english: He describes Them in two verses. “Those two” means the two sages. Their black deerskin and bark are their garments. They have purifying objects in Their hands. The threefold sacred thread is three-stranded, or it is called threefold because the outer purifying rite is described with a ninefold form. They carry the sacred thread and the other articles. “The Veda” means a handful of darbha grass. Moreover, They are austerity itself. Their forms are radiant with a yellow glow like blazing lightning; possessing such brilliance, They appear as embodiments of austerity. “Tall” means elevated.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: उच्चैर् महतादरेण ॥३५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
ते वै भगवतो रूपे नर-नारायणाव् ऋषी ।  
दृष्ट्वोत्थायादरेणोच्चैर् ननामाङ्गेन दण्डवत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
te vai bhagavato rūpe nara-nārāyaṇāv ṛṣī |
dṛṣṭvotthāyādareṇoccair nanāmāṅgena daṇḍavat ||
word_for_word: with the body like a stick
entries.literal_english: With great respect.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: तयोः सन्दर्शनेन य आनन्दस् तेन निर्वृता उपशान्ता आत्मेन्द्रियाशया देहेन्द्रिय-मनांसि यस्य सः । न सेहे नाशक्नोत् ॥३६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
स तत्-सन्दर्शनानन्द- निर्वृतात्मेन्द्रियाशयः ।  
हृष्ट-रोमाश्रु-पूर्णाक्षो न सेहे ताव् उदीक्षितुम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
sa tat-sandarśanānanda- nirvṛtātmendriyāśayaḥ |
hṛṣṭa-romāśru-pūrṇākṣo na sehe tāv udīkṣitum ||
entries.literal_english: The joy produced by seeing Them satisfied and pacified his body, senses and mind. His hairs stood on end and his eyes filled with tears; he was unable to look at Them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: आश्लिषन्न् आलिङ्गन्न् इव ॥३७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
उत्थाय प्राञ्जलिः प्रह्व औत्सुक्याद् आश्लिषन्न् इव ।  
नमो नम इतीशानौ बभाषे गद्गदाक्षरम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
utthāya prāñjaliḥ prahva autsukyād āśliṣann iva |
namo nama itīśānau babhāṣe gadgadākṣaram ||
entries.literal_english: He stood with folded hands and bowed. From eagerness he seemed to embrace Them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: पादयोर् अवनिज्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य । अर्हणेनार्ध्येण ॥३८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तयोर् आसनम् आदाय पादयोर् अवनिज्य च ।  
अर्हणेनानुलेपेन धूप-माल्यैर् अपूजयत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tayor āsanam ādāya pādayor avanijya ca |
arhaṇenānulepena dhūpa-mālyair apūjayat ||
entries.literal_english: He washed Their feet by washing both feet. “With arghya” means with the respectful offering.

entries.sanskrit: पादाभ्यां पादाव् आनम्य । गरिष्ठौ पूज्यतमौ तौ प्रति ॥३९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सुखम् आसनम् आसीनौ प्रसादाभिमुखौ मुनी ।  
पुनर् आनम्य पादाभ्यां गरिष्ठाव् इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
sukham āsanam āsīnau prasādābhimukhau munī |
punar ānamya pādābhyāṃ gariṣṭhāv idam abravīt ||
entries.literal_english: He bowed with his feet to Their feet. “Most venerable” means those two most worthy of worship.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तर्यामिणस् तस्यैव प्राणादि-प्रवर्तकत्वाद् आत्मनः स्तुताव् अस्वातन्त्र्यं पश्यन्न् आह—किम् इति । तव त्वां किम् अहं वर्णये, कथं स्तौमि ? यद् येन त्वयैव उदीरितः प्रेरितोऽसुः प्राणः संस्पन्दते प्रवर्तते, तम् अनु च वाग्-आदयः स्पन्दन्ति । अत्र हेतुः—वै अन्वय-व्यतिरेकाभ्यां, श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं [बृ।आ।उ। ४.४.१८] इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतिभिश् चैतत् प्रसिद्धम् इत्य् अर्थः । न केवलं प्राकृतानां तनु-भृतां किन्त्व् अज-शर्वयोश् च, अतः स्वस्य ममापि तथैव । एवं यद्यपि न कस्यापि स्वातन्त्र्यम्, अथापि दारु-यन्त्रवत् त्वत्-प्रवर्तितैर् अपि वाग्-आदिभिर् भजतां पुंसां भाव-बन्धुर् आत्म-बन्धुर् असि, न तु पित्रादिवद् देह-मात्र-बन्धुः । अहो कृपालुता तवेत्य् अर्थः ॥४०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्री-मार्कण्डेय उवाच—

किं वर्णये तव विभो यद्-उदीरितोऽसुः 

संस्पन्दते तम् अनु वाङ्-मन-इन्द्रियाणि ।

स्पन्दन्ति वै तनु-भृताम् अज-शर्वयोश् च

स्वस्याप्य् अथापि भजताम् असि भाव-बन्धुः ॥
entries.transliteration:
śrī-mārkaṇḍeya uvāca—

kiṃ varṇaye tava vibho yad-udīrito’suḥ

saṃspandate tam anu vāṅ-mana-indriyāṇi |

spandanti vai tanu-bhṛtām aja-śarvayoś ca

svasyāpy athāpi bhajatām asi bhāva-bandhuḥ ||
word_for_word: the intimate friend of the heart
entries.literal_english: Seeing that the Lord within is the mover of the vital airs and the other powers, and recognizing his own lack of independence even while praising the Self, Mārkaṇḍeya says: “What can I describe?” How can I praise You? The vital air moves only when impelled by You, and speech and the other faculties move after it. This is established by the relation of presence and absence and by scriptural statements such as “the ear of the ear.” It is not true only of ordinary embodied beings; it is true also of Brahmā and Śiva, and therefore of me as well. Although no one is independent, You are still the heart’s intimate friend of those who worship You, whose speech and other faculties are moved by You like a wooden puppet. You are not merely a bodily relative like a father; this expresses Your extraordinary compassion.

entries.sanskrit: ननु कथम् आवां प्राणादि-प्रवर्तकौ धर्म-पुत्रत्वाद् आवयोः ? इति चेत्, तत्राह—मूर्ती इति । हे भगवन् ! भगवतस् तव इमे मूर्ती त्रि-लोक्याः क्षेमाय पालनाय ताप-विरमाय च दुःख-निवृत्त्यै मृत्यु-जित्यै मोक्षाय, न तु त्वं कस्यापि पुत्र इत्य् अर्थः । अत्र दृष्टान्तः, यथेदं विश्वम् अवितुम् अन्यास् तनूर् मत्स्य-कूर्मादि-लक्षणा नाना अनेक-प्रकारा बिभर्षि, तद्वत् । न केवलं पालन-मात्रं तव कर्म, किन्तु सृष्टि-लयाव् अपीत्य् आह—सृष्ट्वेति । तत्राप्य् अन्य-निरपेक्षत्वे दृष्टान्तः—ऊर्णनाभिर् इवेति ॥४१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
मूर्ती इमे भगवतो भगवंस् त्रि-लोक्याः

क्षेमाय ताप-विरमाय च मृत्यु-जित्यै ।

नाना बिभर्ष्य् अवितुम् अन्य-तनूर् यथेदं

सृष्ट्वा पुनर् ग्रससि सर्वम् इवोर्णनाभिः ॥
entries.transliteration:
mūrtī ime bhagavato bhagavaṃs tri-lokyāḥ

kṣemāya tāpa-viramāya ca mṛtyu-jityai |

nānā bibharṣy avitum anya-tanūr yathedaṃ

sṛṣṭvā punar grasasi sarvam ivorṇanābhiḥ ||
word_for_word: for the welfare of the three worlds
entries.literal_english: If someone asks, “How can You two be the movers of the vital airs when You are said to be sons of Dharma?”, the answer is: “These forms.” O Lord, these two forms of Yours are for the welfare and protection of the three worlds, for the cessation of suffering and for conquering death—not because You are anyone’s son. Just as You assume many other forms, such as Fish and Tortoise, to protect this universe, so do You here. Your activity is not only protection; You also create and dissolve it. The example shows that You need no other agent: You act like the spider.

entries.sanskrit: यस्माद् एवं-भूतस् त्वं तस्मात् तवाङ्घ्रि-मूलं भजामीत्य् आह—तस्येति । तस्यावितुः पालकस्य स्थावर-जङ्गमानाम् ईश्वरस्याङ्ग्रि-मूलं भजामीति तृतीय-श्लोक-स्थस्यानुषङ्गः । कथं भूतम् अङ्घ्रि-मूलम् । यत्-स्थं यत्र स्थितम् । कर्म-गुण-कालानां रजो-मलम् । अन्ये च पूर्वोक्तास् तपादयो न स्पृशन्ति । “रुजः” इति व पाठः । यतो वेदो हृदये येषां ते वेद-तात्पर्य-विदो मुनयो यद् एव स्तुवन्ति नितरां नमन्ति तद्-आप्त्यै तत्-प्राप्तये एव स्तवनादि कुर्वन्ति ॥४२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यावितुः स्थिर-चरेशितुर् अङ्घ्रि-मूलं

यत्-स्थं न कर्म-गुण-काल-रजः स्पृशन्ति ।

यद् वै स्तुवन्ति निनमन्ति यजन्त्य् अभीक्ष्णं

ध्यायन्ति वेद-हृदया मुनयस् तद्-आप्त्यै ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasyāvituḥ sthira-careśitur aṅghri-mūlaṃ

yat-sthaṃ na karma-guṇa-kāla-rajaḥ spṛśanti |

yad vai stuvanti ninamanti yajanty abhīkṣṇaṃ

dhyāyanti veda-hṛdayā munayas tad-āptyai ||
word_for_word: dust of work, qualities and time
sages who know the heart of the Veda
entries.literal_english: Because You are such a Lord, I worship the root of Your feet. You are the protector, the Lord of the moving and unmoving, and the creator and destroyer. The dust of action, the guṇas and time does not touch one who stands there; the other afflictions described earlier do not touch him either. Those sages whose hearts know the purport of the Veda praise, bow down and worship You solely to attain You. The additional Kaivalya-dīpikā reading explains the feet as belonging to the protector, creator and destroyer; “action” is merit and demerit, “guṇas” are rajas and the others, “time” is death, and these become diseases because they produce transformations. In that reading “n it namanti” is understood through the prefix as hearing or receiving, and “Veda in the heart” means those who know the purport of the Veda; their aim is attainment of Viṣṇu.

entries.sanskrit: यतोऽन्यः पुरुषार्थो नास्तीत्य् आह—नान्यम् इति । अङ्घ्र्य्-उपनयाच् छ्रीमच्-चरण-प्राप्तेर् अन्यं क्षेमं न विद्मः । परितः सर्वेष्व् अपि लोकेषु भीर् यस्य तस्य जनस्य । तद् एवाह—द्वि-परार्धं धिष्ण्यं स्थानं यस्य, स ब्रह्मापि ते कालस्य त्वद्-भ्रू-विजृम्भ-रूपात् कालाद् अलं बिभेति । अतः किम् उत वक्तव्यम् ? तेन ब्रह्मणा कृतानां भौतिकानां प्राणिनां भयम् इति ॥४३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
नान्यं तवाङ्घ्र्य्-उपनयाद् अपवर्ग-मूर्तेः

क्षेमं जनस्य परितो-भिय ईश विद्मः ।

ब्रह्मा बिभेत्य् अलम् अतो द्वि-परार्ध-धिष्ण्यः

कालस्य ते किम् उत तत्-कृत-भौतिकानाम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
nānyaṃ tavāṅghry-upanayād apavarga-mūrteḥ

kṣemaṃ janasya parito-bhiya īśa vidmaḥ |

brahmā bibhety alam ato dvi-parārdha-dhiṣṇyaḥ

kālasya te kim uta tat-kṛta-bhautikānām ||
entries.literal_english: He says that there is no other human goal: apart from attaining the auspicious feet, we know no welfare for a person surrounded by fear. Even Brahmā, whose seat lasts for two parārdhas, greatly fears Your time, which is the expansion of Your brows. Therefore what need be said of the fear of the material beings created by Brahmā?

entries.sanskrit:
यस्माद् एवं तत् तस्मात् तव पाद-मूलं भजामि । कथं-भूतस्य ? ऋत-धियः सत्य-ज्ञान-स्वरूपस्य । यद् वा, सत्या धीर् यस्य यस्मिन् वा तस्यात्म-गुरोर् जीव-नियन्तुर् अतः कारणात् परस्य । किं कृत्वा ? आत्म-च्छदि स्वात्मावरकम् अपार्थं च निष्फलम् असच् च तुच्छम् अन्त्यं च नश् चरम् इदं देहादि हित्वा देहादि-भजनं त्यक्त्वा । असच् चेत् कथं प्रतीयेत ? तत्राह—अभिज्ञ-मात्रम् । न ह्य् अत्यन्तम् असत्, किन्त्व् आत्म-मात्रम् । न ततः पृथग् अस्तीत्य् अर्थः। 

नन्व् अपवर्गाय भवतु मद्-भजनम्, फलान्तरार्थं त्व् अन्य-भजनं कार्यम् एव तत्राह—तर्हीति । यदि त्वां भजति पुरुषस् तर्हि ते त्वत्त एव सर्वं मनीषितम् अर्थं विन्देतेति ॥४४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तद् वै भजाम्य् ऋत-धियस् तव पाद-मूलं

हित्वेदम् आत्म-च्छदि चात्म-गुरोः परस्य ।

देहाद्य् अपार्थम् असद् अन्त्यम् अभिज्ञ-मात्रं

विन्देत ते तर्हि सर्व-मनीषितार्थम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tad vai bhajāmy ṛta-dhiyas tava pāda-mūlaṃ

hitvedam ātma-cchadi cātma-guroḥ parasya |

dehādy apārtham asad antyam abhijña-mātraṃ

vindeta te tarhi sarva-manīṣitārtham ||
entries.literal_english: Therefore, because this is so, I worship Your feet. You are of truthful intelligence, whose nature is true knowledge; alternatively, You are the master of the soul and the controller of the living being, and therefore the Supreme. Having abandoned the body and its adjuncts—the coverings of the self—which are useless, insubstantial, petty and temporary, I worship You. If they are insubstantial, how are they perceived? They are not absolutely nonexistent; they are only the Self appearing as though separate. “Then” answers the objection that another object must be worshiped for another result: if a person worships You, he obtains from You every desired object.

entries.sanskrit: ननु ब्रह्म-रुद्राव् अपि ममैव मूर्ती, अतो माम् एव किम् अत्यन्तम् आद्रियसे ? तत्राह—सत्त्वम् इति । यद् अपि यद्य् अपि तवैव मायया कृट एता लीलास् त्वयैव धृताः, तथापि या सत्त्व-मयी, सैव प्रशान्त्यै मोक्षाय, न केवलम् अस्य प्रशान्त्य्-अभाव-मात्रम् अन्य-भजने किन्त्व् अनिष्टं च भवेद् इत्य् आह—व्यसनेति ॥४५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं रजस् तम इतीश तवात्म-बन्धो

माया-मयाः स्थिति-लयोदय-हेतवोऽस्य ।

लीला धृता यद् अपि सत्त्व-मयी प्रशान्त्यै

नान्ये नृणां व्यसन-मोह-भियश् च याभ्याम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
sattvaṃ rajas tama itīśa tavātma-bandho

māyā-mayāḥ sthiti-layodaya-hetavo’sya |

līlā dhṛtā yad api sattva-mayī praśāntyai

nānye nṛṇāṃ vyasana-moha-bhiyaś ca yābhyām ||
word_for_word: causes of maintenance, destruction and creation
entries.literal_english: Someone might ask: “Brahmā and Rudra are also My forms, so why do you honor Me alone so greatly?” The answer is “goodness.” Although these activities are made by Your Māyā and are assumed by You as pastimes, only the form consisting of goodness is for tranquility and liberation. Worship of the others does not merely fail to give tranquility; it also produces what is undesirable—suffering, delusion and fear.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एव सद्-आचारेण द्रढयति—तस्माद् इति । हे भगवन् ! तव शुक्लां तनुं श्री-नारायणाख्याम् । अथ तावकानां च शुक्लां तनुं नराख्याम् । यद् यस्मात् सात्वताः सत्त्वम् एव पुरुषस्येश्वरस्य रूपम् उशन्ति मन्यन्ते, न त्व् अन्यद् रजस् तमश् चेति । अत्र हेतुः, यतः सत्त्वाल् लोको वैकुण्ट्ःआख्यो लोकत्वे सत्य् अप्य् अभयं च भोगे सत्य् अप्य् आत्म-सुखं च ॥४६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मात् तवेह भगवन्न् अथ तावकानां 

शुक्लां तनुं स्व-दयितां कुशला भजन्ति ।

यत् सात्वताः पुरुष-रूपम् उशन्ति सत्त्वं

लोको यतोऽभयम् उतात्म-सुखं न चान्यत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasmāt taveha bhagavann atha tāvakānāṃ

śuklāṃ tanuṃ sva-dayitāṃ kuśalā bhajanti |

yat sātvatāḥ puruṣa-rūpam uśanti sattvaṃ

loko yato’bhayam utātma-sukhaṃ na cānyat ||
word_for_word: the form of the Supreme Person
entries.literal_english: He establishes this through proper conduct: “Therefore.” O Lord, Your pure form is called Śrī Nārāyaṇa, and the pure form of Your devotees is called Nara. Because the Sātvatas regard goodness itself as the form of the Supreme Person, they do not regard passion or ignorance as such. The reason is that from goodness comes the world called Vaikuṇṭha, which is a world, yet is fearless even though it is an object of experience, and gives the bliss of the self.

entries.sanskrit: अततं प्रणमति, तस्मै नम इति । हंसाय शुद्धाय । संयत-गिरे नियत-वाचे । अथ च निगमेश्वराय वेद-मार्ग-प्रवर्तकाय ॥४७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मै नमो भगवते पुरुषाय भूम्ने 

विश्वाय विश्व-गुरवे पर-देवताय ।

नारायणाय ऋषये च नरोत्तमाय 

हंसाय संयत-गिरे निगमेश्वराय ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasmai namo bhagavate puruṣāya bhūmne

viśvāya viśva-gurave para-devatāya |

nārāyaṇāya ṛṣaye ca narottamāya

haṃsāya saṃyata-gire nigameśvarāya ||
entries.literal_english: He now bows: “Obeisance to Him.” “Haṁsa” means the pure one; “with controlled speech” means one whose speech is restrained; and “Lord of the Vedas” means the one who sets the Vedic path in motion.

entries.sanskrit: वेदार्थ-संप्रदाय-प्रवर्तने हेतुत्वं वदन् स्तौति—यम् इति । वितथाक्ष-पथैः कपटेन्द्रिय-मार्गैर् भ्रमद्-धीर् विक्षिप्त-बुद्धिः पुमान् स्वेन्द्रियादिषु नियन्तृत्वेन सन्तम् अपि यं त्वां न वेद । दृक्-पथेषु विषयेषु । बुद्धि-विक्षेपे हेतुः, तन्-मायया तस्य तवैव मायया आवृता आत्म-निष्ठा मतिर् यस्य स उ सोऽपि आद्य एव पूर्वम् अविद्वान् एवाखिल-गुरोस् तव त्वत्-प्रवर्तितं वेदम् उपसाद्य प्राप्य तं त्वां साक्षाद् वेद ॥४८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यं वै न वेद वितथाक्ष-पथैर् भ्रमद्-धीः

सन्तं स्वकेष्व् असुषु हृद्य् अपि दृक्-पथेषु ।

तन्-माययावृत-मतिः स उ एव साक्षाद्

आद्यस् तवाखिल-गुरोर् उपसाद्य वेदम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
yaṃ vai na veda vitathākṣa-pathair bhramad-dhīḥ

santaṃ svakeṣv asuṣu hṛdy api dṛk-patheṣu |

tan-māyayāvṛta-matiḥ sa u eva sākṣād

ādyas tavākhila-guror upasādya vedam ||
word_for_word: whose understanding is covered by His Māyā
entries.literal_english: He praises Him while stating that He is the cause of transmitting the Vedic meaning and disciplic succession. A person whose intelligence is distracted by deceptive sense-paths does not know You, although You are present as their controller within his own senses and the other objects. His understanding is covered by Your Māyā. Even such a person, originally ignorant, obtains the Veda taught by You, the teacher of all, and then directly knows You.

entries.sanskrit:
वेदेनैव त्वज्-ज्ञानम् इत्य् उपपादयन् प्रणमति—यस्य तव दर्शनं निगमे भवति। कथं-भूतम् ? आत्मनस् तव रहो रहस्यं तस्य प्रकाशकम् । अन्यथा दुर्ज्ञेयताम् अध, अज-परा ब्रह्म-मुख्याः कवयोऽपि साञ्ख्य-योगादिभिर् यतमाना यत्र त्वयि मुह्यन्ति । कुतः ? इत्य् अत आह—सर्वेषां साङ्ख्यादि-वादिनां ये वादास् तेषां विषया भेदादयस् तेषां प्रतिरूपं तत्-तद्-अनुसारि शीलं स्वभावो यस्य तम् । कुतः ? आत्मना देहादि-सङ्घातेन निगूढो बोधो यस्य तम् । एवं-भूतं महा-पुरुषं त्वां वन्दे ॥४९॥

[^५८]:
     आत्म-रहः-प्रकाशं इत्य् अत्र यथा-पदं भा। ३.४.१८,२५-श-पद्य-द्वये द्रष्टव्यम् ॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यद्-दर्शनं निगम आत्म-रहः-प्रकाशं

मुह्यन्ति यत्र कवयोऽज-परा यतन्तः ।

तं सर्व-वाद-विषय-प्रतिरूप-शीलं

वन्दे महा-पुरुषम् आत्म-निगूढ-बोधम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
yad-darśanaṃ nigama ātma-rahaḥ-prakāśaṃ

muhyanti yatra kavayo’ja-parā yatantaḥ |

taṃ sarva-vāda-viṣaya-pratirūpa-śīlaṃ

vande mahā-puruṣam ātma-nigūḍha-bodham ||
word_for_word: whose knowledge is hidden in the self
entries.literal_english: He bows while establishing that knowledge of You comes through the Veda alone. Your vision in the Veda reveals the secret of the Self. Even learned thinkers headed by Brahmā become bewildered while striving through Sāṅkhya, yoga and other systems, because Your nature appears in forms corresponding to the objects of each philosophy. I bow to You, the Great Person, whose knowledge is hidden by the bodily aggregate.
